title: Quartiles and Box Plots

findings.finding: The teaching gives an ogive-estimation procedure, but the guided practice requires an exact discrete median without explaining the change of procedure.
findings.breakdown: For p28-q3, half the total is 19, but the 19th and 20th observations are 21 and 22. Reading only the prescribed halfway position does not supply their average, 21.5.
findings.checked: Earlier teaching supplies medians of ordered observations. The opening review asks students to recall cumulative-frequency medians, but its answer working is not permanent teaching. The new key ideas and example do not distinguish graph estimates from exact discrete summaries.
findings.assumptions: Students retain the earlier median-of-halves method; calculator access is immaterial.

repair.proposal: After p27-key-ideas, add: 'Use the ogive for estimates. For exact summaries of individual scores, use cumulative column heights to locate the middle observation or observations in the whole dataset and in each half.' Make the p28 instruction request exact summaries. Beside p28-q3, add: 'Locate the 19th and 20th scores separately, then average them for the median.'

findings.doneWhen: The teaching distinguishes estimation from exact rank-based summaries before guided practice.

findings.finding: The final question moves directly from reading complete distributions to reverse quartile reasoning with two missing cumulative frequencies and a minimum constraint.
findings.breakdown: Students must infer a quartile from the known IQR, translate its rank into a cumulative-frequency bound, and minimise an unknown bar. The preceding questions practise only forward readings.
findings.checked: No supplied earlier question bridges the reverse rank-to-frequency decision. The closing challenge combines several changes rather than introducing one new feature.

repair.proposal: Before p30-q5, insert: 'A dataset contains 50 integer scores, all at least 15. Its cumulative frequency at 15 is 4, and its lower quartile is 16. What is the smallest possible cumulative frequency at 16?' Answer: 13, because the lower half contains 25 observations and its median is the 13th observation.

findings.doneWhen: Students encounter one reverse quartile-to-frequency task before the combined challenge.

protectedGroups.observation: The positional scaffolds show when a quartile is a single observation and when it is the average of two observations.
protectedGroups.varies: Dataset size and the resulting odd or even size of each half.
protectedGroups.invariant: Find the overall median, form the two halves, then find each half's median.

protectedGroups.observation: Moving every value equally changes the median but preserves range and IQR.
protectedGroups.varies: All five feature positions increase by one.

protectedGroups.observation: Moving the maximum can change range without changing median or IQR.
Changing an upper quartile changes IQR while range and median remain fixed.
The median can change without changing either measure of spread.
The middle half can become less spread out while the overall range stays fixed.
protectedGroups.varies: Q1 and Q3 move inward equally.

protectedGroups.observation: The subtraction follows the quartile labels rather than the order in which the givens appear.
protectedGroups.varies: Values and the presentation order of Q1 and Q3.

protectedGroups.observation: An odd dataset excludes its central observation when forming halves; an even dataset splits between its central observations.
protectedGroups.varies: Dataset parity and the corresponding splitting instruction.
protectedGroups.invariant: Find the median of each half, then subtract Q1 from Q3.

protectedGroups.observation: Percentages depend on the quartile regions covered, including differently positioned intervals containing the same proportion.
protectedGroups.varies: Interval endpoints and the number of quartile regions included.

protectedGroups.observation: The same age interval can contain different proportions of different populations; combined counts come from adding the subgroup counts.
protectedGroups.varies: Population, quartile coverage and population total, followed by aggregation.

protectedGroups.observation: Approximately symmetrical distributions can have different concentrations in their central half, so symmetry alone cannot determine the match.
protectedGroups.varies: Relative central concentration and box width compared with the whiskers.

protectedGroups.observation: Equal ranges do not imply equal IQRs, medians or shapes.
protectedGroups.varies: Median, quartiles, IQR and skewness between the two samples.
